subject: Banking
title: Forex Market Rigging
description: A quick, practical guide to Forex Market Rigging.

hook.text: Banks rigged the $6.6 trillion-a-day foreign exchange market.

buildup.text: Currency rates are 'fixed' daily at 4 PM London time. Banks used the fixing window to manipulate rates for profit.

discovery.text: Traders coordinated via Bloomberg chat rooms. They shared client orders and timed trades to move the fix in their favor.

twist.text: Six banks paid $5.6 billion in fines. But no senior executives went to prison.

climax.text: Forex rigging showed that traders will collude whenever supervision is weak.

punchline.text: 'The Cartel.' $5.6 billion in fines. The forex market was rigged for years.

quiz.question: What were the chat rooms used by forex-rigging traders called?

details.summary: Traders at major banks colluded in chat rooms with names like The Cartel to manipulate foreign exchange benchmarks, rigging the $6.6 trillion daily forex market for years before being caught and fined billions.
details.whyItMatters: The forex market affects the cost of everything that crosses borders. Rigging it means banks were secretly taxing international trade, pensions, and investment funds that rely on honest exchange rates.
takeaways: Traders coordinated in private chat rooms to rig currency benchmarks
Five major banks paid over $5.7 billion in combined fines
The manipulation affected the 4pm London fix used globally

faq.question: How did traders rig forex benchmarks?
faq.answer: Traders from competing banks shared client order information in private chat rooms, then coordinated large trades in the seconds before the benchmark was set to push prices in their favor.

faq.question: Who was affected by forex manipulation?
faq.answer: Anyone holding foreign currency or international investments was affected. Pension funds, multinational corporations, and even travelers exchanging money all paid slightly manipulated rates without knowing it.
